_doc: Central parameter file. robotino: robot, motors, omni contact and the Robotino surface library (also the base library of every other robot: any surface can be used by any robot, and other libraries extend it through "base"). rover: the MarsSim rover. Surface groups (_kind): calibrated = identified on the real robot, synthetic / extreme / hard = built from handbook values on top of a calibrated surface. Every _doc says where the numbers come from.

robotino._doc: Robotino 1.6 (3 omni wheels), firm-ground Bekker-Wong-Janosi omni contact; robot, motors and the four "calibrated" surfaces identified on 576 recorded runs of the real robot (4 floors x 72 directions x 0.1-0.3 m/s)

gray._doc: gray rubber mat (calibrated on recorded runs: run means and 0.5 s windows)

green._doc: green plastic turf (calibrated on recorded runs)

table._doc: table, chipboard (calibrated on recorded runs); mu is not identifiable (the wheels stay far from the friction limit), fixed at 1.0

red._doc: red EVA mat (calibrated on recorded runs); mu is not identifiable, fixed at 1.0

table_wet._doc: chipboard / laminate with a water film: the calibrated table with mu 1.0 -> 0.35 (rubber on a wet smooth surface 0.3-0.4); compliance K and losses as the table

carpet._doc: carpet, 6 mm pile on a rigid base: the pile compresses by ~2.5 mm under the wheel (p ~130 kPa) and recovers by 75 %; the rollers sink into the pile (f_lat between green and gray), pile shear K as green

carpet_shag._doc: shag carpet, 15 mm pile: compresses by ~6 mm (40 %), recovers by 70 %; the rollers sink into the pile (f_lat above gray), pile shear K 10 mm, rubber-on-fibre friction 0.9

foam._doc: soft polyurethane foam mat, 20 mm: linear foam (n = 1), sinkage ~6 mm, hysteresis 20 % (rebound 0.8); friction and shear as the calibrated EVA mat

sand_lete._doc: dense LETE sand (Wong; Project Chrono): kc 102 kN/m^(n+1), kphi 5301 kN/m^(n+2), n 0.793, c 1.3 kPa, phi 31.1 deg, K 12 mm

sandy_loam._doc: sandy loam, 15 % moisture (Wong, LLL): kc 5.27 kN/m^(n+1), kphi 1515 kN/m^(n+2), n 0.7, c 1.72 kPa, phi 29 deg, K 25 mm. Robotino (8 cm wheels, 11 kg) gets stuck: 3-8 % of the commanded speed, slip ~1

clay_wet._doc: wet clayey soil, 38 % moisture (Wong, Thailand): kc 13.19 kN/m^(n+1), kphi 692.2 kN/m^(n+2), n 0.5, c 4.14 kPa, phi 13 deg, K 10 mm. Robotino (8 cm wheels, 11 kg) gets stuck: 3-8 % of the commanded speed, slip ~1

mars_soil._doc: Mars soil simulant of MarsSim (Zhou et al. 2023, Table II): kc 13.6 kN/m^(n+1), kphi 2259.1 kN/m^(n+2), n 0.92, c 462 Pa, phi 35 deg, K 15 mm, the same soil as for the rover. Robotino gets stuck (sinkage 13 mm, ~8 % of the speed): the soil was measured for 14 x 20 cm rover wheels

tile._doc: glazed ceramic tile, dry: hard smooth base, losses and K as the calibrated table; mu 0.6 (rubber / polyurethane on dry glazed tile 0.5-0.7, handbook). Joints between tiles are not modelled

linoleum._doc: linoleum (PVC), dry: hard smooth base, losses and K as the table; mu 0.7 (rubber on dry linoleum 0.6-0.9, handbook)

concrete._doc: trowelled concrete, dry: hard base, losses and K as the table; mu 0.8 (rubber on dry concrete 0.6-0.85, handbook)

gray_wet._doc: the calibrated gray rubber mat with a water film: roller losses and K as the dry mat (same rubber hysteresis); mu 1.35 -> 0.5 (rubber on wet rubber 0.4-0.6, handbook)

green_wet._doc: the calibrated green plastic turf, wet: losses and K as the dry turf; mu 0.54 -> 0.3 (rubber on wet plastic 0.25-0.4, handbook)

ice._doc: ice near 0 C: hard smooth base, losses and K as the table; mu 0.1 (rubber / polyurethane on ice 0.05-0.15, handbook)

rover._doc: MarsSim six-wheel rocker-bogie rover (Zhou et al., IEEE TAES 2023, Table II); geometry not published in the paper was identified on the paper experiments
